title: What If Abdul El-Sayed Became President?

beats.text: What if Abdul El-Sayed became president? The first fight might start before he signs a single law. Would America see a president or a Muslim man it has been told to fear?

That is hypothetical. El-Sayed is running for Senate in Michigan not the White House. But Donald Trump has called him a jihadist and questioned his loyalty. El-Sayed rejected those attacks as baseless.

Now imagine he wins. His platform calls for Medicare for All and getting corporate money out of politics. Private health insurers could face a very different future and a massive fight over who pays for care.

But winning the Oval Office would not make those promises law. Congress would still have to pass them. A president can demand change but he cannot simply order the entire healthcare system to change overnight.
So the real question is bigger than one election. Could he win the country and then convince Congress to let him govern?
